newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 11.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest -June 11.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - French media group Havas says it appoints Eric Licoys as senior executive vice president with responsibility for implementing strategic decisions taken by the board and chairman Pierre Dauzier. (Reuter)

PARIS - The appointment of Eric Licoys as managing director of Havas will help Havas to carry out its aggressive strategy, Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier tells financial daily newspaper La Tribune Desfosses. (Reuter)
ALGIERS - The Algerian government is using its hold on advertising by the public sector to put economic pressure on privately-owned newspapers. (Le Figaro)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET

PARIS - Recent comments by the new French Communication and Culture Minister, Catherine Trautmann, show she is sticking by her plans for media reforms, but she is not going to rush into taking hasty decisions, an adviser at the culture ministry said.(Reuter)
PARIS - Worries over possible changes to laws governing ownership of French media companies are already reflected in the companies' share price, dealers say. (Reuter)
PARIS - French public television channel France 2 does not need to engage in a "stupid race" for audience with private channel TF1, says Jean-Pierre Cottet, France 2 managing
director.(Reuter)

PARIS - The number of subscribers to French cable television services rose 11.78 percent to 1.53 million at the end of April from 1.37 million a year earlier, according to the Association des Villes Cablees, the "association of cabled towns". (La Tribune)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS
PARIS - French carmaker Renault commissions an independent study to explore alternatives to the proposed closure of the Vilvoorde assembly plant that sparked an outcry in France and Belgium.
(Reuter)
PARIS - Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer says the group continues to target breakeven for its car operations. (Reuter) *********

PARIS - A Paris court orders the chairman of French tobacco company Seita and three Dutch executives of Rothmans to pay damages to the French anti-smoking body, the Comite National Contre le Tabagisme, for not having the correct health warning on cigarette packets. (Le Parisien)
CONSUMER TRENDS:

TURIN - Despite the strong 43.2 percent jump in Italian new car registrations in May, the overall European car market slipped 0.5 percent to 1,156,200 units, provisional data from Italian carmakers' association Anfia show. (Reuter)

PARIS - The bottle of red wine is disappearing from French dinner tables. Only one in two French wine drinkers now drink wine regularly, while the other half only drink it with guests, according to studies carried out since 1980. (Le Parisien)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
